chunks: Al-Khalil ibn Ahmad al-Sejezy narrated to me, saying: Umar ibn Hafs narrated to us, saying: Suleiman ibn al-Ash'ath narrated to us, saying: Yazid ibn Khalid al-Ramli narrated to us, saying: Ibn Wahb narrated to us, from Abi Hani, from [Abi] Abd al-Rahman al-Hubli, from Jabir ibn Abdullah, saying:
The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) mentioned beds, saying: A bed for the man, a bed for the woman, and a bed for the guest. The fourth is for Satan.
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the fourth bed in Islamic household etiquette?
ai.summary: In *Al-Khisal*, Shaykh al-Saduq records this hadith to illustrate the Prophetic etiquette (*adab*) regarding domestic space, where the fourth bed is attributed to Satan not merely as a physical object but as a symbol of unnecessary clutter or distraction that disrupts household harmony. This teaching reflects the Shia emphasis on maintaining a spiritually pure and orderly environment, where excess can invite spiritual negligence (*ghaflah*). The attribution to Satan highlights how mundane domestic arrangements can have significant metaphysical implications in Islamic thought.
